extracted.intended_audience: general news readers and journalists interested in media ethics and reporting standards
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practices for reporting and editing serious allegations (especially sexual-assault reporting) including verification, attribution, giving subjects a chance to respond, and corrective actions when failures occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to basic journalistic practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporting must follow 'basic, even routine journalistic practice' in gathering, verifying, and presenting facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columbia's review concluded the article violated routine practices; this is a broad expectation that underpins the more specific criteria below.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify quoted-attributions by contacting quoted individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters should contact and confirm quotations attributed to named or described individuals before publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columbia found Erdely 'didn't try to contact three of Jackie's friends, who later denied quotations attributed to them' — failing to contact attributed speakers is a clear lapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make an independent effort to identify and corroborate people in anecdotes
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters must independently identify people mentioned in anecdotes and seek corroboration rather than relying solely on the principal source's account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steve Coll called the reporter's failure to make 'an independent effort to identify those three people' the 'point of failure.' Editors should ensure reporters pursue independent identification and corroboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent attribution of speech and sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly indicate when dialogue or descriptions come from a single source, and avoid presenting secondhand speech as if it were directly quoted from those allegedly quoted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The review criticized editorial choices that 'hid from readers the fact that they got this speech from Jackie, not from any of the three' — transparency about source origin is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide subjects and organizations an adequate chance to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: Before publication, give accused individuals, named organizations, or groups a fair and adequate opportunity to respond to allegations attributed to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Columbia found 'The magazine didn't give Phi Kappa Psi... an adequate chance to respond.' Failure to seek comment from implicated parties undermines fairness and reporting credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify alleged perpetrators when necessary to enable investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: When allegations involve specific alleged attackers, reporters should take reasonable steps to identify them (or explain why they cannot) so authorities can investigate and the public can assess claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rolling Stone 'never identified Jackie's alleged attackers, making it impossible for police to effectively investigate the case.' There are safety/ethical trade-offs, but identification or clear explanation is required for investigative viability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sole reliance on a single uncorroborated source for serious allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not publish major allegations based solely on one person's account without independent corroboration or sufficient documentary evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Erdely acknowledged she 'did not go far enough to verify her story' and relied on confidence in the source; the piece shows the risk of single-source reporting on high-stakes claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance concern for vulnerable sources with rigorous verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Protecting sources from re-traumatization and treating victims with sensitivity must not substitute for necessary questioning and fact-gathering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Erdely said she allowed 'my concern for Jackie's well-being, my fear of re-traumatizing her, and my confidence in her credibility to take the place of more questioning and more facts.' Newsrooms should employ trauma-aware techniques while still pursuing verification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial accountability and oversight for attribution and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors must critically review reporters' sourcing, attribution choices, and verification steps, and not accept reporting trails that lack identification or corroboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report faulted editors for accepting a reporting trail that 'failed to identify and hear from these three' and for choices that obscured sourcing; editors share responsibility for lapses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrective actions: retract, apologize, and commission independent review when failures occur
rubrics_metrics.description: When reporting is found to have serious, systemic failures, publications should retract or correct the story, apologize to those harmed, and consider commissioning an independent review of editorial processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rolling Stone retracted the article, apologized to readers and those damaged, and published an independent Columbia report — the article presents these steps as appropriate responses to major journalistic failures.
